themes.title: Tiere
themes.subtitle: Animals
themes.desc: 60 animals from pets to sea creatures — with article, plural and CEFR level.
themes.intro: Animals are one of the easiest ways into a language: short, concrete, and you already know the concept. Learn them with their article (der/die/das) and plural, because that is what German actually tests.
notes: Every animal noun is capitalised — that is not a typo, all German nouns are.
Learn the article with the word: der Hund, die Katze, das Pferd. Gender is what most learners get wrong.
das Tier (animal) is the general word; das Haustier is a pet.
The plural of most animals here adds -e or -en: der Hund → die Hunde, die Katze → die Katzen.
A few stay identical in the plural: der Hamster → die Hamster, das Zebra → die Zebras.

themes.title: Farben
themes.subtitle: Colours
themes.desc: 14 colours with the exact shade and the CEFR level.
themes.intro: Colours are adjectives, and German adjectives change their ending depending on what they describe. Learn the base colour first; the endings come later.
notes: Colours are adjectives: das rote Auto (the red car), die rote Tür (the red door).
With sein the colour stays plain: Das Auto ist rot.
hell- = light, dunkel- = dark: hellblau (light blue), dunkelgrün (dark green).

themes.title: Zahlen
themes.subtitle: Numbers
themes.desc: Numbers from 0 to a million, plus the ordinals you need for dates.
themes.intro: Numbers are everywhere: prices, times, addresses, phone numbers. German builds them from the back — einundzwanzig is literally 'one-and-twenty'.
notes: Numbers 21–99 are said backwards with und: 21 = einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty).
eins becomes ein- when joined: einundzwanzig, einhundert.
sechs and sieben shorten: sechzehn, siebzig.
Ordinals for dates: am dritten Mai (on the third of May).

themes.title: Körper
themes.subtitle: The body
themes.desc: 26 body parts with article and plural — the words you need at the doctor.
themes.intro: Body parts come up constantly: at the doctor, describing pain, buying clothes. German uses der/die/das here too, and the plural matters.
notes: Body parts are often used with the definite article, not a possessive: Ich habe mir das Bein gebrochen.
At the doctor: Mein Kopf tut weh. (My head hurts.) — wehtun is the verb for pain.
der Zahn → die Zähne: watch the umlaut in the plural.

themes.title: Kleidung
themes.subtitle: Clothing
themes.desc: 20 items of clothing with article and plural — for shopping and weather talk.
themes.intro: Clothing vocabulary pairs with shopping and weather. German nouns here often change vowel in the plural (das Hemd → die Hemden), and a few add -er.
notes: die Hose and die Jeans are singular in German but plural in English: Die Hose ist neu.
Shopping: Ich hätte gern… (I'd like…) and Wie viel kostet das?
anziehen = to put on, ausziehen = to take off, tragen = to wear.

themes.title: Zeit
themes.subtitle: Time
themes.desc: Weekdays, months and seasons — the calendar words you use every day.
themes.intro: Days, months and seasons are the backbone of scheduling. In German, weekdays and months are nouns, so they take a capital letter, and 'on' is am.
notes: Weekdays and months are capitalised: am Montag, im Januar.
'on' a day = am: am Dienstag. 'in' a month/season = im: im Sommer.
morgen (tomorrow, lowercase) vs der Morgen (the morning, a noun).
Seasons: im Frühling, im Sommer, im Herbst, im Winter.

themes.title: Essen und Trinken
themes.subtitle: Food and drink
themes.desc: 40 foods and drinks, from staples to sweets.
themes.intro: Food is one of the first topics you actually use: shopping, ordering, cooking. Most food nouns carry their article, and a few are plural-only like die Nudeln.
notes: Food nouns are der/die/das words: der Käse, die Milch, das Brot.
die Nudeln is plural-only, like English 'pasta'.
Uncountable things take no plural: das Wasser, der Reis, das Mehl.
Meals: das Frühstück, das Mittagessen, das Abendessen.

themes.title: Obst und Gemüse
themes.subtitle: Fruit and vegetables
themes.desc: 28 fruits and vegetables — the words you meet at the market.
themes.intro: Market vocabulary is concrete and easy to picture. All of these are nouns with an article, and most take an -n or umlaut plural.
notes: der Apfel → die Äpfel: many fruit words take an umlaut in the plural.
die Kartoffel is a vegetable in German, not a 'fruit'.
At the market: ein Kilo Tomaten, bitte (a kilo of tomatoes, please).
das Obst (fruit) and das Gemüse (vegetables) are collective nouns with no plural.

themes.title: Im Restaurant
themes.subtitle: At the restaurant
themes.desc: 26 words and phrases for ordering, eating out and paying.
themes.intro: Eating out needs vocabulary and set phrases. Learn the menu words first, then the polite sentences — they are fixed and worth memorising whole.
notes: Ich hätte gern… is the polite way to order — softer than Ich will.
der Kellner / die Kellnerin — waiter and waitress.
Stimmt so means 'keep the change'.
Zum Mitnehmen = to take away; hier essen = to eat in.

themes.title: Küche und Geschirr
themes.subtitle: Kitchen and dishes
themes.desc: 23 appliances, pots and tableware.
themes.intro: The kitchen is full of everyday nouns, and German compounds them freely: der Kühlschrank is literally 'cool cupboard'.
notes: German loves compounds: der Kühlschrank = kühl (cool) + Schrank (cupboard).
The article follows the last part: die Spülmaschine is feminine because die Maschine is.
das Geschirr and das Besteck are collective nouns — no plural.

themes.title: Haus und Möbel
themes.subtitle: House and furniture
themes.desc: 31 rooms, furniture and parts of the home.
themes.intro: Home vocabulary pairs with prepositions: in der Küche, auf dem Tisch, an der Wand. Learn the noun and its preposition together.
notes: Rooms take in + dative: in der Küche, im Bad.
Furniture is often der: der Tisch, der Stuhl, der Schrank.
der Boden is the floor you walk on; die Erde is soil/earth.
Compounds again: das Schlafzimmer = Schlaf (sleep) + Zimmer (room).

themes.title: Familie und Menschen
themes.subtitle: Family and people
themes.desc: 30 family members and people around you.
themes.intro: Family words are the first nouns most learners meet. Note that German marks gender in the word itself: der Freund (male friend) vs die Freundin (female friend).
notes: die Eltern and die Geschwister are plural-only.
das Mädchen is neuter despite meaning 'girl' — because of the -chen ending.
Adding -in makes a female form: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin, der Freund → die Freundin.
der Freund can mean 'boyfriend', die Freundin 'girlfriend' — context decides.

themes.title: Verkehrsmittel
themes.subtitle: Transport
themes.desc: 25 vehicles and travel words, from the bus to the plane.
themes.intro: Getting around needs both the vehicle and the verb: mit dem Bus fahren, in den Zug einsteigen. Learn them as pairs.
notes: Travel takes mit + dative: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn.
einsteigen = to get on, aussteigen = to get off.
die U-Bahn = Untergrundbahn (underground), die S-Bahn = Schnellbahn (fast rail).
Ich habe eine Verspätung — the train is late.

themes.title: Stadt und Orte
themes.subtitle: Town and places
themes.desc: 30 places in town — where to shop, bank, post and park.
themes.intro: Town vocabulary lets you ask for and give directions. Many of these are compound nouns, and the article follows the last part.
notes: Asking the way: Wo ist…? / Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?
die Post and die Polizei have no plural.
Compounds take the last part's gender: das Rathaus (das Haus), die Buchhandlung (die Handlung).
auf dem Markt (at the market) — places use in/auf/an + dative.

themes.title: Natur und Landschaft
themes.subtitle: Nature and landscape
themes.desc: 29 words for the natural world — plants, water, land and sky.
themes.intro: Nature words show up in weather talk, travel and reading. A few are plural-only, like die Alpen.
notes: der See = lake, but die See = sea. Gender changes the meaning!
der Wald → die Wälder: umlaut plus -er in the plural.
Nature nouns are mostly der: der Baum, der Berg, der Fluss.
die Erde is both the planet and soil.

themes.title: Wetter und Jahreszeiten
themes.subtitle: Weather and seasons
themes.desc: 30 weather words and the phrases you use to talk about it.
themes.intro: Weather is the classic small-talk topic. German uses es ist for most weather: Es ist kalt, Es ist sonnig.
notes: Weather uses es: Es regnet, es schneit, es ist kalt.
der Regen (noun) → es regnet (verb) → regnerisch (adjective).
das Eis means both 'ice' and 'ice cream' — context decides.
Seasons: im Frühling, im Sommer, im Herbst, im Winter.

themes.title: Berufe
themes.subtitle: Jobs
themes.desc: 32 jobs with the female form for each.
themes.intro: Job titles take -in for women: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin. When you state a profession, German drops the article: Ich bin Lehrer.
notes: Stating a job takes no article: Ich bin Lehrer. (not ein Lehrer).
Feminine forms add -in: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin, der Arzt → die Ärztin.
der Angestellte / der Beamte behave like adjectives (ein Angestellter).
Was sind Sie von Beruf? = What do you do for a living?

themes.title: Schule und Lernen
themes.subtitle: School and learning
themes.desc: 31 school words and study verbs.
themes.intro: School vocabulary is essential for anyone studying in German. Note die Schule vs der Unterricht — the building vs the lesson.
notes: lernen = to learn (school), studieren = to study at a university.
School subjects take no article: Ich habe Mathe.
die Hausaufgabe is usually used in the plural: die Hausaufgaben.
eine Prüfung machen / bestehen = to take / pass an exam.

themes.title: Büro und Arbeit
themes.subtitle: Office and work
themes.desc: 28 words for the workplace, meetings and contracts.
themes.intro: Work vocabulary is useful for job applications and office life. die Arbeit is the general word; der Beruf is your profession.
notes: arbeiten als + job: Ich arbeite als Ingenieur.
arbeiten bei + company: Ich arbeite bei Siemens.
einen Termin vereinbaren = to arrange an appointment.
die Bewerbung → sich bewerben (to apply).

themes.title: Computer und Internet
themes.subtitle: Computers and internet
themes.desc: 30 words for technology, devices and the online world.
themes.intro: Tech vocabulary is mostly borrowed from English, but German often keeps its own word too: der Computer or der Rechner.
notes: das Handy is a false friend — it means 'mobile phone', not 'handy'.
der Rechner is a native German word for computer.
herunterladen and hochladen are separable: Ich lade die Datei herunter.
das Passwort → die Passwörter: umlaut in the plural.

themes.title: Länder und Nationalitäten
themes.subtitle: Countries and nationalities
themes.desc: 44 countries and the nationality words that go with them.
themes.intro: Countries are mostly neuter and take no article: Ich komme aus Deutschland. A few need one, like die Schweiz and die Türkei.
notes: Most countries take no article: Ich komme aus Deutschland.
Exceptions: die Schweiz, die Türkei, die USA, die Niederlande — these need one.
'from' = aus for countries, aus der for the feminine ones: aus der Schweiz.
Languages take no article: Ich spreche Deutsch.

themes.title: Gefühle
themes.subtitle: Feelings
themes.desc: 36 words for emotions and how to express them.
themes.intro: Feelings are adjectives with sein: Ich bin müde. For 'to be afraid of', German uses Angst haben vor.
notes: Feelings take sein: Ich bin traurig.
Ich freue mich = I'm glad; sich freuen auf = to look forward to.
Angst haben vor + dative: Ich habe Angst vor Hunden.
Es tut mir leid is the standard apology.

themes.title: Charakter und Aussehen
themes.subtitle: Character and appearance
themes.desc: 41 adjectives to describe people — looks and personality.
themes.intro: Describing people needs adjectives for both appearance and character. In German these take endings before a noun: ein freundlicher Mann.
notes: Adjectives take endings before nouns: ein freundlicher Mann, die freundliche Frau.
After sein there is no ending: Er ist freundlich.
Er hat braune Haare — note the -e ending on the adjective.
groß = tall/big; for people it means tall.

themes.title: Körperpflege
themes.subtitle: Personal care
themes.desc: 24 words for daily routines and hygiene.
themes.intro: Daily routine vocabulary pairs with reflexive verbs: sich waschen, sich anziehen. Most are separable and use sich.
notes: Reflexive verbs need sich: Ich wasche mich.
sich die Zähne putzen — the body part takes the definite article, not a possessive.
sich anziehen is separable: Ich ziehe mich an.
Ich dusche mich or simply Ich dusche — both are fine.

themes.title: Gesundheit und Arzt
themes.subtitle: Health and the doctor
themes.desc: 30 words for illness, symptoms and seeing a doctor.
themes.intro: Health vocabulary is essential if you live in Germany. The key verb is wehtun: Mein Kopf tut weh (my head hurts).
notes: wehtun is separable: Mein Kopf tut weh. (My head hurts.)
Body parts take the definite article: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen, not meine.
Most pain words are plural-only: die Kopfschmerzen, die Bauchschmerzen.
Gute Besserung! = Get well soon!

themes.title: Sport und Hobbys
themes.subtitle: Sport and hobbies
themes.desc: 30 sports, hobbies and the verbs that go with them.
themes.intro: Sport and hobby words let you talk about free time. Many sports are nouns, and some are just verbs: Ich schwimme gern.
notes: Sport machen or Sport treiben = to do sport.
Ich spiele Fußball — but Ich mache Yoga (no spielen for non-ball sports).
gern shows you like it: Ich schwimme gern.
gewinnen → gewann → gewonnen (irregular).

themes.title: Musik und Kunst
themes.subtitle: Music and art
themes.desc: 26 words for music, film, art and culture.
themes.intro: Culture vocabulary is great for talking about free time. Instruments are die or das, and you play them with spielen.
notes: You play instruments with spielen: Ich spiele Klavier.
Ich gehe ins Kino (cinema) or ins Konzert (concert).
der Schauspieler → die Schauspielerin for the female form.
auftreten is separable: Die Band tritt heute auf.

themes.title: Kommunikation
themes.subtitle: Communication
themes.desc: 28 words and phrases for talking, writing and phoning.
themes.intro: Communication covers talking, writing and telephoning. Many phrases are fixed and worth learning as whole blocks.
notes: Sie (capital) is formal 'you'; du is informal.
anrufen is separable: Ich rufe dich an.
sprechen → du sprichst (vowel change in the du form).
Formal greetings: Guten Morgen (until ~11), Guten Tag (day), Guten Abend (evening).

themes.title: Feste und Feiertage
themes.subtitle: Festivals and holidays
themes.desc: 24 words for celebrations, holidays and greetings.
themes.intro: German culture has many festivals. Learn the festival name plus the greeting: Weihnachten → Frohe Weihnachten!
notes: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag! is the full birthday greeting.
Frohe Weihnachten (Christmas) and Frohes neues Jahr (New Year).
Ich gratuliere dir! = Congratulations to you!
Weihnachten and Ostern have no plural.

themes.title: Richtungen und Wege
themes.subtitle: Directions and routes
themes.desc: 24 words for asking and giving directions.
themes.intro: Directions combine prepositions with dative/accusative: gehen Sie geradeaus, biegen Sie links ab. Learn the phrases whole.

words.en: How do I get to the station?

words.de: Es ist ganz in der Nähe.

words.en: the first street on the left

notes: Wie komme ich zu…? = How do I get to…? (always zu + dative).
Biegen Sie ab — abbiegen is separable.
links and rechts can mean both 'left/right' and 'on the left/right'.
in der Nähe = nearby; weit weg = far away.

themes.title: Small Talk
themes.subtitle: Small talk
themes.desc: 24 questions and answers for everyday conversation.
themes.intro: Small talk is the fastest way to sound natural. These are fixed formulas — memorise them as whole sentences and swap in your own details.

words.en: What are you doing at the weekend?

notes: Use Sie with strangers and du with friends and family.
Freut mich! is the standard 'nice to meet you'.
Gern! means 'gladly' — a friendly yes.
Es geht so = 'so-so' — not bad, not good.

themes.title: Geld und Einkaufen
themes.subtitle: Money and shopping
themes.desc: 26 words for money, prices and shopping.
themes.intro: Shopping vocabulary covers money, prices and the shop itself. Prices use Euro and Cent, and 'costs' is kostet.
notes: Wie viel kostet das? is the key shopping question.
teuer = expensive, günstig / billig = cheap.
Ich hätte gern… is the polite way to ask for something.
mit Karte zahlen = pay by card; bar zahlen = pay cash.

themes.title: Formen und Maße
themes.subtitle: Shapes and measures
themes.desc: 22 words for shapes, sizes and measurements.
themes.intro: Shapes and measures come up in descriptions and shopping. German uses the metric system, and adjectives like rund stay plain after sein.
notes: Wie groß ist…? asks about size or height.
After sein, adjectives stay plain: Der Tisch ist rund.
Units don't pluralise after a number: zwei Meter, drei Kilo.
die Größe is also clothing size: Welche Größe haben Sie?

themes.title: Umwelt und Klima
themes.subtitle: Environment and climate
themes.desc: 28 words for the environment, climate and sustainability.
themes.intro: Environment is a core B2 topic, common in exams and news. Many nouns are compounds with -schutz, -müll or -energie.
notes: Compounds are everywhere: der Umweltschutz (Umwelt + Schutz), der Mülltrennung (waste separation).
Müll trennen = to separate rubbish — a German habit.
Der Klimawandel is masculine; die Erderwärmung is feminine.
Useful verb: etwas für die Umwelt tun = to do something for the environment.

themes.title: Gesellschaft und Politik
themes.subtitle: Society and politics
themes.desc: 30 words for society, politics and current affairs.
themes.intro: Society and politics appear in B2/C1 exams and news. These nouns are mostly abstract, and many are compounds with -ung.
notes: die Regierung, die Wahl, die Partei — most politics nouns are feminine.
wählen means both 'to vote' and 'to choose'.
eine Entscheidung treffen = to make a decision.
Ich bin der Meinung, dass… = In my opinion… (good for essays).

themes.title: Medien und Nachrichten
themes.subtitle: Media and news
themes.desc: 25 words for media, news and communication.
themes.intro: Media vocabulary helps you follow the news in German. die Nachrichten is plural-only — the news.
notes: die Nachrichten is plural: Ich sehe die Nachrichten.
in den Medien = in the media (dative plural adds -n).
eine Zeitung lesen, Nachrichten schauen.
der Journalist → die Journalistin for the female form.

themes.title: Unregelmäßige Verben
themes.subtitle: Irregular verbs
themes.desc: 45 strong verbs with their three principal forms.
themes.intro: Strong verbs change their stem vowel. The three forms — infinitive, Präteritum, Perfekt — are what you memorise: gehen → ging → ist gegangen.
notes: The three forms: Infinitiv – Präteritum – Perfekt: gehen – ging – ist gegangen.
Strong verbs change the stem vowel; weak verbs add -te and ge-…-t.
Verbs of motion take sein in the Perfekt: Ich bin gegangen.
Most take haben: Ich habe gegessen.

themes.title: Trennbare Verben
themes.subtitle: Separable verbs
themes.desc: 29 separable verbs and their prefixes.
themes.intro: Separable verbs split: the prefix goes to the end. aufstehen → Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf. The prefix is stressed.
notes: Separable prefixes are stressed: AUFstehen. Inseparable ones are not: verSTEHen.
In the main clause the prefix goes to the end: Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf.
With zu, it goes between: Ich habe vor, früh aufzustehen.
Inseparable prefixes: be-, ge-, er-, ver-, zer-, ent-, emp-, miss-.

themes.title: Verben mit Präpositionen
themes.subtitle: Verbs with prepositions
themes.desc: 27 verb + preposition pairs with their case.
themes.intro: Many German verbs need a fixed preposition, and the case depends on it. Learn the pair as one unit: warten auf + accusative.

words.de: Ich freue mich auf den Urlaub.
words.en: I'm looking forward to the holiday.

words.de: Ich nehme an dem Kurs teil.
words.en: I'm taking part in the course.

words.de: Ich danke dir für deine Hilfe.
words.en: I thank you for your help.

notes: Learn the verb with its preposition as one unit: warten auf, not just warten.
auf and an can take accusative (movement) or dative (position).
For people/things, use da(r)-: Ich warte darauf.
Worauf wartest du? = What are you waiting for?

themes.title: Nomen mit Präpositionen
themes.subtitle: Nouns with prepositions
themes.desc: 24 fixed noun + preposition pairs.
themes.intro: Nouns also carry fixed prepositions, usually with Angst vor, Lust auf. Learn them with the noun.
notes: Angst haben vor + dative: Ich habe Angst vor Hunden.
Lust haben auf + accusative: Ich habe Lust auf Eis.
The noun keeps its own preposition: die Antwort auf die Frage.
With da(r)-: Ich habe Angst davor.

themes.title: Adjektive mit Präpositionen
themes.subtitle: Adjectives with prepositions
themes.desc: 26 adjective + preposition pairs.
themes.intro: Adjectives carry fixed prepositions too: stolz auf, zufrieden mit. These are common in exams.
notes: Learn the adjective with its preposition: stolz auf, zufrieden mit.
Ich bin stolz auf dich. (accusative) vs Ich bin zufrieden mit dir. (dative).
Many take mit + dative: zufrieden mit, verheiratet mit.
Ich bin daran interessiert. — with da(r)- for things.
